title: Cost Per Mile Calculator
description: Turn any journey's total cost into a per-mile figure with the Cost Per Mile Calculator — the honest comparison for trips and vehicles. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a $455 road trip over 850 miles costs $0.54 per mile — the number that tells you what the same trip costs next year, whatever its route.
quick_answer: The Cost Per Mile Calculator divides a journey's or a vehicle's total cost by the miles covered and returns the per-mile figure. Enter the total spend and the distance and read the unit cost — the honest way to compare two trips, two cars or a car against the train.

faq: What costs can I include?
Fuel, tolls, parking, hire charges, wear — your consistent list. The figure means what your categories say it means; keep them the same across comparisons.
Is this a tax mileage rate?
No. Tax and employer rates are published allowances; this is your actual unit cost computed from your actual spend. The two are compared, not confused.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. This is cost accounting over a completed or planned distance; traffic belongs to the ETA tools.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads follow terrain and networks, not geometry. Cost follows the road figure — the miles your wheels actually turned.
Can route results change over time?
Costs drift with fuel prices and tolls; recompute per period. The division itself never changes.
How do I get cost per kilometre instead?
Divide the total by kilometres, or use the Cost Per Kilometer Calculator — its answers convert at 1.609344 km per mile.
Should depreciation be included?
For a vehicle's true cost per mile, yes — it is often the largest term. For a trip's marginal cost, no. Decide which question you are answering.
One-way or round trip?
Use the miles the wheels turned — usually the round trip. A one-way figure for a journey you also drove back understates the truth by half.
Does it work for a bicycle or on foot?
The division works for any mode with a cost and a distance; the categories (cake, shoe leather) are yours to price.
How often should I recompute?
Per fuel-price era or per vehicle change. A figure older than a price shock is history, not data.
